questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

I can’t __make out__ my mind about taking a vacation in winter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"make up"**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the **phrasal verb **is incorrect.
 
• A phrasal verb is a combination of a **verb **and **preposition**, adverb, or sometimes both.
 
• The meaning of a phrasal verb may vary significantly from its literal meaning.
 
• The meaning is not formed from the individual words but in their combined usage.
 
• Let's look at the given phrasal verbs.
 
• **Make up**: to make a decision about something.
 
• **Made out**: assert or imply something about a particular person or thing.
 
• **Make on**: to turn on, light, or ignite
 
• As per the meaning of given phrasal verbs, "**make up**" is the appropriate word choice.
 
 
• **Example**: *Rajat can't **make up**__ his mind about whether to pursue medicine or engineering*.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker has to take a decision regarding the vacation, so "make up" is appropriate.

**The correct sentence is: ***I can’t __**make up**__** **my mind about taking a vacation in winter.*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**

• We use the preposition '**of**' usually to talk about quantification, the relation of an object with a noun, and for reference.

• We use the preposition '**at**' to talk about time, location or activity.

**The correct sentence is**:* He was formerly a doctor __**at **__the corporate hospital.*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 4.**

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. They always shared machinery and goods as needed without a hitch.

B. Then they had the first serious quarrel in 40 years of farming side by side.

C. And unfortunately, the long collaboration fell apart.

D. Two brothers lived on adjoining farms in a small village.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**DABC**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement D **is the opening sentence of the passage as it begins by giving the **background **of the story. The story is about two brothers who lived on adjoining farms in a small village.
 
• **Statement A **is the second sentence of the passage as it **continues **the story of the two brothers who always shared machinery and goods as needed without a hitch.
 
• **Statement B **is the third sentence of the passage as it begins with "**then**" which marks a moment in time. In the given sentence, we are told about the first time the brothers had a quarrel.
 
• **Statement C** is the last sentence as it begins with the conjunction "**and**" which links the previous statement to this one. It also talks about the consequence of the quarrel mentioned in the previous sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is** option 1.**

**The correct passage is: D. **Two brothers lived on adjoining farms in a small village. **A. **They always shared machinery and goods as needed without a hitch. **B**. Then they had the first serious quarrel in 40 years of farming side by side. **C**. And unfortunately, the long collaboration fell apart.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The rule is: **Present Indefinite + Time expression= Present Perfect**.
 
• Some of the important Time expressions are:
 
 
• For (period of time)
 
• Since (point of time)
 
 
 
• For example:
 
 
• Monika has known me for two months. (“two months” is a period of time)
 
• Monika **has known** me **since** 1995. (“1995” is a point of time)
 
 
 
• In this question,** 'since' **is the **point of time **that is used here. Hence, the **present perfect tense** is appropriate here.
 
• Thus, 'has lived' must replace 'lived' (past tense).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Smita **has lived **in this house since she was five years old.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**
